source.title: On Inductive Biases That Enable Generalization of Diffusion Transformers
source.authors: Jie An; De Wang; Pengsheng Guo; Jiebo Luo; Alexander G. Schwing

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies generalization in diffusion generative models, but none of the listed versions covers its denoising task or measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports PSNR gaps and FID for diffusion models and attention-window changes. These results concern image-distribution modeling, not the listed random-label capacity, classifier architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example claims. It reports no random-label experiment.
record.test_reason: The study measures diffusion-model denoising PSNR gaps and generation FID. None of V1–V8 names these comparisons. Local attention in a diffusion transformer does not test V3's convolutional versus fully connected classification claim. The doubled-batch comparisons also change seeds and dataset splits and do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors associate diffusion-transformer generalization with attention locality and show that local attention, its placement, and effective window size modify PSNR gaps. They also conclude that DiTs outperform equivalent-FLOP UNets on this gap with limited data despite lacking harmonic Jacobian bases, and that improved gaps often accompany better FID under limited data.
record.recipe_differences: Diffusion generative modeling with pixel-space DiT and UNet backbones, trained on natural image datasets; interventions restrict attention windows or reduce parameters. The source is a preprint, not a reproduction of the listed classifier studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-set size; backbone size; dataset; attention-window placement; effective window size; local-window distribution; random seed, data shuffle, and batch size in † comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: At equivalent FLOPs, DiT has smaller PSNR gaps than UNet with 10^3 or 10^4 training images; both have small gaps with 10^5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pixel-space diffusion transformers can have smaller denoising train-test gaps than equivalent-FLOP UNets when training data are limited.

fits_no_version.finding: Local attention reduces diffusion PSNR gaps across six datasets and two backbones; early placement and smaller effective windows are more favorable, while mix or tail placement can worsen gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention locality affects diffusion-transformer denoising generalization, depending on placement and effective window size.

fits_no_version.finding: Local attention improves FID with 10^4 training images, while effects at 10^5 are mixed. R15 requires the configuration and value corrections above.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local attention can improve diffusion generation quality under limited training data, with effects depending on configuration and data quantity.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter sharing slightly reduces PSNR gaps; PCA-composed attention does not reduce them and can worsen them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested parameter-reduction approaches provide less improvement in diffusion-transformer generalization than local attention.

fits_no_version.finding: UNet Jacobian eigenvectors exhibit geometry-adaptive harmonic patterns with sufficient data; DiT eigenvectors do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometry-adaptive harmonic Jacobian representations are not necessary for the denoising generalization exhibited by the tested diffusion transformers.

record.code_released: Source code will be released publicly upon paper publication. Project page: dit-generalization.github.io/
record.problems: The main PSNR-gap comparisons are shown in figures without numerical values in the text. Comparisons use three dataset-shuffled models for Fig. 2; other uncertainty estimates are not stated. The paper studies diffusion image modeling, so its outcomes do not directly test the listed classifier versions.
record.rows_left_out: FID table rows for additional datasets, backbones, seeds, and placements are omitted to prioritize reported PSNR-gap results and keep row coverage concise; see Tables 1–3 and Appendix C Table 5. FID summaries are mentioned in fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out classification versus natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, including learned sparse local connections and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recovery through recipe changes.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking of classification generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because no row measures a listed effect; this does not imply that the reported diffusion comparisons lack readable directions. FID uses training images as its reference distribution, so it is not held-out classification performance. The paper cites generalization literature but neither tests nor operationally uses a listed finding.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps of one-hidden-layer ReLU classifiers.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers trained from scratch.
Large-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and classifier train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring classifier test accuracy.

rows.value: Reducing window size decreases PSNR gap; exact values figure only
rows.note: The related FID results are reported in Table 3 but are not the PSNR-gap measure.
rows.check: The intervention is misdescribed. Table 4's smaller-window variant replaces three additional global layers, giving local side lengths (3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19) followed by three global layers. Its comparator is the six-local-layer Local configuration. Measures no listed version.

rows.value: Increasing window size increases PSNR gap; exact values figure only
rows.note: Authors say larger windows diminish generalization.
rows.check: The diffusion PSNR-gap increase measures no listed version. Table 4 specifies enlarged local side lengths (5,5,5,7,7,7,9,9,9).

rows.note: Authors describe the distribution change as having limited impact.

rows.subject: DiT-XS/1 w/ Local Attn (5×6)
rows.operation_detail: Used six local attention layers, each with window size 5×5.
rows.note: Values are for N=10^4 and N=10^5 in that order. FID improves at N=10^4 but is mixed at N=10^5.
rows.check: Values are assigned to the wrong configuration. Table 3 gives Local Attn (5×6) FID as CelebA 12.9798 and 2.3348, ImageNet 40.7373 and 17.8686, for N=10^4 and 10^5 respectively. Its paired window-distribution comparator has values 12.6680, 2.3455, 40.7499 and 17.7538. The recorded values belong to Local (head), duplicating R16. FID measures no listed version.

rows.subject: DiT-XS/1 w/ Local (head)
rows.operation_detail: Placed six local windows in early layers.
rows.note: Values for early placement are also listed in Table 1; at N=10^4 FID decreases, while N=10^5 results vary by dataset.
rows.check: The FID values match Table 2, but measure no listed version. This row combines three improvements and one deterioration and should be separated if directional diffusion findings are retained.

rows.subject: DiT-XS/1 with parameter sharing
rows.operation_detail: Second and fourth DiT blocks reused parameters of the first and third blocks.
rows.value: Parameter sharing reduced PSNR gap but was not as effective as local attention; exact values figure only
rows.note: Authors explicitly characterize the improvement as less effective than local attention.
rows.check: Parameter-sharing effects on diffusion PSNR gaps measure no listed version. Appendix C describes a reduction, while the Figure 12 caption characterizes it as slight.

rows.subject: DiT-XS/1 with PCA-composed attention maps
rows.operation_detail: Replaced first three self-attention maps with maps composed from principal components.
rows.value: PCA composition did not reduce PSNR gap and may make it worse; exact values figure only
rows.note: The text says the method cannot reduce the gap.
rows.check: PCA-composed attention effects on diffusion PSNR gaps measure no listed version. Fifty principal components describes the representation, not the model's parameter count.
